questions.stem: A client with an acute asthma exacerbation has received repeated inhaled bronchodilator therapy. The client is now drowsy, speaks only single words, has minimal air movement, and the oxygen saturation is falling. What should the nurse do?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Continue the same intermittent treatment schedule and reassess in one hour because reduced wheezing usually indicates that bronchospasm is resolving.","B":"Escalate emergency respiratory care immediately, continue acute asthma treatment, and prepare for advanced airway support if respiratory failure progresses.","C":"Have the client walk to improve ventilation and obtain a peak-flow value before notifying the provider, because objective testing should precede escalation.","D":"Withhold supplemental oxygen until an arterial blood gas is obtained because oxygen can obscure the severity of airflow obstruction during assessment."}}
questions.rationale: Drowsiness, inability to speak normally, worsening hypoxemia, and markedly reduced air movement during an asthma exacerbation are high-risk features for impending respiratory failure. Current GINA guidance requires urgent escalation and intensive treatment rather than delayed reassessment or exertional testing. Supplemental oxygen should not be withheld from a hypoxemic patient.
questions.source_name: Global Initiative for Asthma — 2026 GINA Strategy Report
questions.source_detail: 2026 GINA guidance covers acute severe asthma and urgent escalation when clinical features indicate life-threatening exacerbation or impending respiratory failure.

questions.stem: An adult has partial-thickness thermal burns involving about 12% of total body surface area, including part of the face and one hand. After initial stabilization, which disposition is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Routine primary-care follow-up because partial-thickness burns require burn-center consultation only when more than 20% of total body surface area is involved.","B":"Discharge with topical therapy because involvement of the face and hand does not affect referral decisions when the total burn area remains below 15%.","C":"Admit to a standard medical unit without burn consultation because burn-center referral is reserved for full-thickness injury or electrical burns.","D":"Obtain burn-center consultation with consideration for transfer because this burn size and involvement of the face or hand meet referral criteria."}}
questions.rationale: The American Burn Association recommends immediate consultation with consideration for transfer for partial-thickness burns involving at least 10% TBSA and for deep partial- or full-thickness burns involving critical areas such as the face or hands. This client meets a referral threshold by burn size and has high-risk anatomic involvement.
questions.source_name: American Burn Association — Burn Patient Referral Guidelines
questions.source_detail: Immediate consultation/consideration for transfer is recommended for partial-thickness burns at least 10% TBSA and for significant burns involving the face or hands.
